# Small-cap sizing native reference

Original OPC/XML controls, generated by `python tools/canvas_small_caps_sizes_fixture.py`. Export `public/fixtures/small-caps-sizes.docx` to `native.pdf` with the reference application, then run `python tools/record_small_caps_sizes_reference.py`. No third-party template engine or template content is used; fonts are referenced by name and are not redistributed as application assets.

The reference application renders 162 cases across Times New Roman, Arial and Calibri. Each font covers half-point steps from 1 to 24.5pt, then 30, 36, 48, 72, 96 and 144pt. Latin, accented Latin, Greek and Cyrillic uppercase/lowercase pairs, digits and punctuation distinguish reduced glyphs from full-size ones.

Every measured lowercase glyph agrees with 80% of the stored size, rounded to the nearest half point, with a 1pt minimum. Uppercase, digits and punctuation keep the stored size. The recorded expectations are PDF font sizes, not values generated by that formula. The reference application's PDF font quantization accounts for deviations of up to 0.06pt (for example 13pt appears as 12.96pt).

This differs from ECMA-376 Part 1 §17.3.2.33, which specifies a two-point reduction. The engine follows the independent native reference measurements. Original source text, UTF-16 offsets, stored font size, kerning threshold decisions, and package XML remain unchanged. Subscript/superscript and width transforms still apply after capitalization sizing.

The unit and browser checks compare every glyph's size against the retained native reference; browser checks also cover actual canvas painting, editing, export/reopen, original download and exact undo. They establish sizing behavior, not complete font shaping fidelity across platforms.
